method: Spoke length is solved in two steps with the cosine rule and Pythagoras. The in-plane distance C from the hub spoke hole to the rim spoke hole is sqrt(R^2 + r^2 - 2Rr cos(theta)), where R is the effective rim radius (ERD / 2), r is the hub flange radius (flange diameter / 2) and theta is the lacing angle, 720 degrees divided by the holes per flange times the number of crosses -- 67.5 degrees for a 32-hole 3-cross wheel and 60 degrees for 36-hole 3-cross. The spoke length is then sqrt(C^2 + w^2) - h/2, where w is the lateral distance from the hub centreline to the spoke bed -- the flange-to-centre distance plus the rim offset on the left and minus it on the right, because an offset spoke bed sits towards the right flange and a rim fitted the other way round swaps the two sides -- and h is the spoke hole diameter, because the nipple takes up half the hole diameter of thread. Left and right flanges are solved separately. Spokes are sold in 1 mm steps, so each side is rounded to the nearest whole millimetre and the purchase advice follows the usual wheel-building rule: use one length when the sides agree, the longer length when they differ by 1 mm, the average at 2 mm, and two separate lengths at 3 mm or more. Inputs are limited to measurable ranges (ERD 200-800 mm, 8-48 even spoke holes, 0-4 plus crosses up to a quarter of the hole count, flange 20-120 mm, flange offset 0-80 mm, hole 0-6 mm, rim offset 0-30 mm); blank, non-numeric, odd and out-of-range values are rejected with an actionable message. The model assumes J-bend spokes, evenly spaced holes and a spoke bed radius of ERD / 2, so straight-pull hubs, offset drilling, hub motors and unevenly spaced holes need their own dimensions, and measured rim and hub values should always be confirmed against a known build. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Spoke length geometry: cosine rule on the flange radius, rim radius and lacing angle, then Pythagoras with the flange offset, less half the spoke hole diameter (Sheldon Brown, Measurements for Bicycle Spoke-Length Calculations)
